decisions: before the first edit: spec and design said any dimension on a resource-less operation fails startup, which would forbid OBJECT on reconciliation.run.start - the very case object scope exists for. Corrected both: a resource-less operation admits ALL or OBJECT (OBJECT is bound by the @AdminObject parameter, not by rows).

1.1-1.5 were implemented together: the starter cannot compile between them (AdminOperation, AdminGrants, ScopePolicies are removed as one cut). Each task's own tests ran in the final pass: OperationCatalogTest, OperationGrantsTest, OperationAuthorityTest, OperationScopeValidatorTest, OperationEnforcementMvcTest (new), plus every admin test rewritten to operation ids. mvn -pl :security-spring-boot-starter install: 240 tests, 0 failures.

Design deviation (D3): the DataScopeProvider SPI keeps its (principal, resource, action) signature instead of taking an Operation. OperationAuthority asks providers with the operation's scopeResource()/scopeAction(): its resource and action, or for an operation touching no rows its id and the new Operation.INVOKE action. Every SPI implementer (identity projection, export, test-support, the crud WATCHER provider) is untouched, and an object grant for reconciliation.run.start is keyed (reconciliation.run.start, invoke) instead of (admin.reconciliation, operate).

DataAccessGuard depends on a new data.ScopeLookup interface (resourceOf, scopeFor) that OperationAuthority implements, so row enforcement does not depend on the operation package (no data<->operation cycle). Its audit/metric action is now the operation id.

@EnableMethodSecurity moved from DataAuthorizationAutoConfiguration to the new OperationAutoConfiguration, so ludwig.security.data.enabled=false no longer turns method security - and with it @RequiresOperation on business methods - off. RequiresOperationAuthorizationManager evaluates BUSINESS operations; on an ADMIN one it only confirms the surface bound exactly that operation (AdminInvocation), so a call that bypassed the surface is refused and one that came through it is not evaluated twice. With ludwig.admin.enabled=false a still-mapped admin handler is therefore 403, not served.

AdminInvocation.open is public but takes only an Authorization, which only OperationEvaluator can construct, keeping 'nothing unauthorized can be bound' now that the evaluator lives in security.operation.

web-core is optional for the security starter: the description check moved behind an OperationDescriptions bean registered only with web-core, and discovery is @ConditionalOnClass as well. Known limit: the reason-required and PAT refusals throw web-core problem types, so in a service without web-core those refusals fail closed as a 500 rather than a 400/403.
CompositeDataScopeProvider resolves its members on first use: with the policy provider gone, Spring's fallback offered the composite itself as its only candidate during creation (circular reference).
hasPermission(target, permission) now takes an operation id, denied when the object's class is not that operation's resource. No code used it.

RemovedOperationKeys fails startup when ludwig.admin.grants, ludwig.security.data.policies, data.default-access, data.strict-policy-tokens or ludwig.admin.allow-personal-access-tokens is still set, naming the replacement - binding would otherwise ignore them silently.

For group 2: every area module's auto-configuration was conditional on the AdminOperationCatalog bean as 'the admin surface exists'; OperationCatalog now exists whenever security does, so those conditions must move to AdminSurfaceGuard (and job-core's ReplicaControlAutoConfiguration likewise).

1.6: security README EN+RU rewritten: 'Resource level' became 'Operations and roles' (operation model, ludwig.security.roles, sensitivity/surface, discovery and holders), data level on operation ids and per-subject providers (the README example no longer calls principal.hasRole), admin surface on Operation.admin/@RequiresOperation, object scope via OBJECT and OperationAuthority.admitted, config block, adoption steps (no allow-everything mode), runbook/decision rows. Heading parity 20/20. docs/data-scope-configuration.md (EN+RU) still documents the old policies: added to 4.1's scope. OperationAuthority.admitted(principal, operation, objects) replaces AdminObjectScope.filter for listings (reconciliation is the one user); 241 tests.
